label: text

SPANISH TROOPS MOROCCO
LANDING.

label: paragraph_title
text: ... (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: It is officially announced that the Spaniards have effected a lending at Albuernes.

label: text
text: General Primo di Rivera has sent a wireless message to the King from the battleship "Alfonso Thirteenth" that troops commanded by General Suro funded on the peninsula of Morromuevo on the western side of the bay of Albuemus at noon and established a position half an hour later after a short bombardment without great resistance.

label: text
text:
HOW IT WAS DONE.
Paris San

label: text
text:
The Journal's Madrid corros-
pondent states that preparations for
the Spanish landing at Albuccano
began on Saturday evening when
Spanish naval detachments escorting troops ships left Costa and
Molila, respectively.

label: text
text: The detachment from Central Tainted a landing south of Wudhu, which is south of Temar, and then wont full speed to Albucerna.

label: text
text: The detachment from Melilla founded a landing at Sidirriss, then joined the Conta detachment, which was reinforced by French warships. The false landings were intended to mislead the Riffs as regards the real object of the attack.

label: text
text: An intense bombardment of the coast was carried out on Sunday evening by French and Spanish washships supported by the air force, and on Monday morning a landing of troops which was attempted only resulted in costly losses, as the Riffs were prepared for the landing, and offered determined resistance.

label: paragraph_title
text: EARTH RACEANS.

label: text
text: "Les Journal's" Madrid correspondent says that the attempted landing of Spanish troops on the Albucense coast failed. "The attempt will be repeated today. The Biff coast is being located by land, sea and air.

label: text
text: Tangier, despite its "invention" serious Rift counter operations, in the western front directed by Abd al Krim's brother, the enemy vainly endenvouring to capture Benkarrish, just south of Tetuan, while on the eastern front the enemy is strongly counter attacking on the African front east of Ajdir and Alliecenas.

label: text
text: A telegram from Fez refers to a rumour that the Spaniards succeed in relieving enemy pressure on Petunia. A Spanish official communiqué makes no reference to any attempted landing at Almeens but dwells on the persistent enemy pressure, especially on the western front and declares that the enemy failed in their object of breaking the Spanish lines with the ultimate aim of diverting the forces destined for the offensive.

label: paragraph_title
text: INDIA'S PROBLEMS.

label: text
text: SWARAJISTS AND INDEPEN. DENTS UN THE.

label: text
text: VICTORY IN TUE ASSEMBLY.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: That the British in India is accused of being merely thieves and robbers was one of the bitter tauts against the Government whose administration practically all Indian speakers condemned when the Assembly resumed the debate on Sir Alexander Muddman's resolution and Mr. Motilal Nelur's amendment advocating that the total responsibility of the Government be invested in the legislature with transitional reservations in respect of this army and foreign affairs.

label: text
text:
The amendment was eventually passed by 72 votes to 45.
Sir Alexander Muddiman described the amendment as a virtual repeat of the Government of India Act. He admitted that as denoting for the first time the Swarajists and independents were agreed it deserved the utmost attention.

label: text
text:
India's fitness to govern herself was urged by Mr. Motilal Nehru when the Legislative Assembly discussed Sir Alexander Nuddiman's resolution proposing acceptance of the majority report of the reforms enquiry committee regarding which Sir Alexander Nuddman advised the House to follow the Viceroy's advice urging co-operation which would solve "one of the greatest problems of the human race." Mr. Motilal Nehru moved an amendment whereby the constitution and administration would be fundamentally changed, declaring Indians looked for a place in the sun for themselves. Ho strongly urged that a convention representing all interests should finance scheme for the approval of the legislature to be submitted to the British Parliament and embodied in the Statute Book.
Hankow, Sept. 8, — Land and water demonstrations took place today. There was no incident and all was carried out in the most orderly manner.

Reuter

label: paragraph_title
text: HOSTILE SCENES.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: The shipowners have decided to post notices giving the men 24 hours to consider the position and stating that failing compliance with certain terms they will be compelled to take strong action. There will be no victimisation if crews will obey orders.

label: text
text: The shipowners state that they have been tolerant throughout, but they cannot submit to further dictation.

label: text
text: Hostile scenes by the strikers abroad two stenances in Table Buy were seen when the "Roman Star" loaded with a record cargo of 100,000 cases of citrus fruit, was leaving the docks. There were improvements, threats and frequent cries of "Blackleg I"

label: text
text: It is understood the "Roman Star" crew put to sea under an arrangement with the fruit ex-elango ensuring them their old terms.

label: text
text: SIGNIFICANT

label: text
text: An important development of the strike occurred with the sailing of the muize ship "Gothland" with the majority of her original crew who wearied at the length of the strike.

label: paragraph_title
text: MAIZE SHIPS.

label: paragraph_title
text: Capetown, Sept. 9

label: text
text: The strikers have agreed with Colonel Creswell, the Labour Minister, that in order to prevent congestion of the maize export and consequent unemployment of dock labourers, maize vessels shall be taken from the jetties into the roadstead, provided a guarantee is given that the ships will not put to sea without the crews' consent.

label: text
text: The shipowners decline to give a general undertaking.

label: text
text: The strikers by arrangement with the Government ballotted regarding the sailing of the fruit ship "Roman Star." The ballot resulted in 432 to 352 votes against sailing.

label: paragraph_title
text: YESTERDAY'S BASEBALL.

label: text
text: The “friendly” baseball match between the Japanese and a team from a U.S.S. “Helena” at the Happy Valley diamond yesterday afternoon had a thrilling finish, the sailors accomplishing the seemingly impossible by making the necessary number of runs in the last inning to draw level.

label: text
text: The sides were evenly matched, excellent pitching and fielding holding the sides down to a blank score for the greater part of the game and runners getting no further than third base.

label: text
text: The Japanese opened the score in the fifth inning through Kusano and S. Hachiuma on a fly by. Uno. In the next inning Y. Hachiuma put his side further up by getting Yokoi home.

label: text
text: The sailors entered their last inning with a three runs' deficit. They scored this number amid deafening cheers from their supporters. A faulty throw at third base proved lucky for the "gobs" and assisted in the making of the first two runs.

label: text
text: The Japanese failed in their last inning and the match ended in a draw.

label: text

INFANTRYMEN NOVICE
TOURNEY.

label: text
text: "HERMES" V. THE REGIMENT.

label: text
text: A Navy and Marines champion and this year's belholder, in the person of Able Seaman Ewin of H.M.S. "Hermes" will be boxing at Murray Barracks, in the open-air ring, on Saturday night.

label: text
text:
Ewin comes with a good reputation from Home and it was once said that he was a likely opponent for Marine Belts, the local champion. However, Ewin was defeated by A. B. Jackson (H.M.S. "Hawkins") in a three rounds (Imperial Services) bout on the "Hermes" last Saturday.
This week-end, the "Hermes" is sending a team to try conclusion with the Surrey Regiment. Boxing starts at 8.30 p.m. Reserved seats $1, unreserved 50 cents, service-men in uniform, half price. Booking through R. S. M. Maynard. Murray Barracks.

LIEUT. LIVOCK MAKES BUNS.

label: text
text: Flight Lieut. G. E. Livock, who kept wicket and opened the battling for Malaya in the last series of triangular interport cricket matches played here, has now appeared for the Gentlemen in first-class cricket at Home.

label: text
text: Before the interport matches were played here last year, it was announced in the "China Mail" that Mr. Livock had already appeared for Lord Cowdray's XI against England. He did not do himself full justice in Hongkong during the stay of the seaplane carrier, H.M.S. "Pegasus" but he made a century against Kowloon. When presented with a bat to commemorate the fent he expressed himself as preferring a golf club. He hardly played any cricket here except in the triangular interport and it was thought by a few that he might desert the game.

label: text
text: This season the “China Mall” reported that Mr. Livock had appeared with distinction for a Middlesex club and had played for the metropolitan county in first-class matches.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: With two other representative matches being played simultaneously it was only to be expected that some unusual names would crop up in the Folkestone match. From a perusal of the result it will be seen that England's best cricketers were split up into several teams, the strongest of which might have been either of those playing at Scarborough. It should be noted that Dick Tyldesley, who turned out for his county at Blackpool, was one of the M.C.C. XI in Australia.
